title: After a loss: judge decisions, set process goals
outcomes: Separates the result of a game from the quality of a decision
Tells process goals from outcome goals
Writes a short after-loss routine and a stopping rule in advance

steps.text:
A result mixes your decisions, your opponent's decisions and luck. After a loss it is easy to blame yourself for everything or for nothing. A habit to try: judge the **decisions** (what you control) separately from the **result**.
This lesson makes no claim about feelings or about what raises ratings.

steps.title: Result and decision are different things
steps.prompt: Judge the decision, not what happened afterwards. Predict, then check.

steps.text: A **process goal** is something you can do whether or not you win: 'run the safety scan on every move', 'write one unsure moment per game'. An **outcome goal** depends on your opponent: 'win', 'reach 1500'. Process goals are specific, in your control and checkable afterwards. They are a habit to try, not a proven method.

steps.prompt: Sort these four goals into process goals and outcome goals.

fields.label: Run the safety scan on every move
Write one unsure moment after each game

steps.text: **After a loss, a three-step routine to try:** 1. Write one thing you did well. 2. Write one decision you would change and what you could see when you made it. 3. Choose one thing to do differently next session. Do this on paper before you look at an engine or a rating.

steps.prompt: Use your most recent loss or bad session. Fill in the routine in plain words.

fields.label: One decision I would change, and what I could see then:
One thing I will do differently next session:

steps.text:
**Decide your stopping rule in advance.** For example: stop for the day after two losses in a row. No number is proven; pick one and test it.
The app does not see games you play on other sites, so nothing here runs unless you start it. If a loss leaves you feeling much worse than a game should, talk to someone you trust. That matters more than chess.

steps.prompt: Set your plan. Silent practice for your next session: write down whether you met your process goal before you look at your rating or the result.

fields.label: My process goal for the next session:
I will write the result of the process goal:
